transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-11 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Seastar), Owen Hart (Seastar), Jules Park (Seastar security)
---
Summary:
- Intro: PLG quicklaunch and free credits to get to first token.
- Main asks: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs; security requirements (SOC2, KMS, audit logs); expected throughput, latency and cost targets.
- Agreed next steps: send security docs, run small benchmark, propose pilot scope and credits redemption flow.
---
Topics: Quickstart credits, time-to-first-token, hosting fit, VPC private pilot, benchmarks, cost per 1k tokens, compliance
---
Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros. i'm maya from redwood, diego is our systems engineer.
[00:00:17] Priya (Seastar): hey, priya here. product lead for search and assistant features. we've been poking around the API docs.
[00:00:26] Owen: owen, platform, i'll be the hands-on for infra.
[00:00:30] Jules: jules on security.
[00:00:33] Diego (Redwood SE): nice to meet you all. super quick agenda: credits/onramp, hosting options, security, then next steps. sound good?
[00:00:45] Priya: yep, perfect. our main goal is time-to-first-token; we want something engineers can prototype in a day. also—we have some enterprise constraints so we want to see hosted first but maybe private later.
[00:01:04] Maya: right. so the PLG quicklaunch path gives you free credits to spin up calls against the hosted API, we usually see teams hit their first real request within a couple hours.
[00:01:18] Priya: couple hours? okay, that's promising. what do you mean by hosted though—like fully managed with logs retained?
[00:01:27] Diego: hosted is our managed API on our control plane, logs are available in the console for a limited retention, and you can opt-in to longer retention add-on. important note: payloads are ephemeral unless you opt into storing conversation history.
[00:01:45] Jules: can you clarify data encryption in transit and at rest? and KMS support?
[00:01:52] Diego: yes TLS in transit, at rest encryption is supported, and we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can discuss bring-your-own-KMS for dedicated/private. there was a small hiccup in our doc text where K-V cache got written as K-V cash — that's a doc typo.
[00:02:18] Owen: ha, i saw that. ok. our throughput target is around 30 rps peak for generation with average response under 600ms for short prompts. is that feasible on hosted?
[00:02:34] Diego: depends on model/seq length. for short prompts with a 1k token budget, hosted with autoscaling and burst capacity typically meets that, but if you need strict latency SLOs we recommend dedicated pools where you reserve a GPU fleet and get predictable tails.
[00:02:56] Priya: how big of a delta are we talking cost-wise? hosted cheaper initially?
[00:03:03] Maya: hosted is usage-based and lower upfront, but dedicated locks you into reserved capacity — better for steady high-throughput to lower unit cost. we'll share a cost sheet.
[00:03:17] Priya: and private/VPC—what's the lift?
[00:03:21] Diego: private is more setup (VPC peering, IAM, KMS integration, possibly on-prem hardware). typical lift is 2-6 weeks depending on access and approvals. we have a private on-prem bundle if you need air-gapped.
[00:03:39] Jules: our compliance requirement: SOC2, ISO27001, SSO via SAML, audit logs, and the ability to rotate keys via our HSM. will those be met?
[00:03:50] Maya: yes we are SOC2 and have ISO artifacts; for SAML SSO we support SAML OIDC flows. HSM integration is supported in Private; for hosted we can discuss HSM-backed KMS with a contract. i'll drop the security pack after this call.
[00:04:05] Priya: great. about quickstart credits—what's the redemption flow? can non-admin engineers use them?
[00:04:13] Maya: credits are attached to an account and can be used by any API key created in that account. typical path: we create a promo code, you redeem it in the console, you get X dollars of usage, and we point you to the quickstart repo for examples.
[00:04:30] Owen: do you have SDKs? our stack is node + go.
[00:04:34] Diego: yes official SDKs for node, python, go, plus open-telemetry hooks and a small quickstart repo with sample prompts.
[00:04:44] Priya: okay, technical question: does Redwood keep kv-cache across requests if we use session ids? we rely on prefix caching for multi-turn.
[00:04:53] Diego: we do prefix/KV caching, and the runtime manages the KV cache—there's an option to pin cache to a model variant. small note the transcription in the docs sometimes says 'KV cash' — ignore.
[00:05:07] Priya: noted.
[00:05:11] Owen: any limits on streaming? we stream tokens to clients today.
[00:05:15] Diego: we support streaming and function calling, same as the docs. for heavy streaming loads we recommend testing with our benchmarking runner because it can change throughput patterns.
[00:05:29] Priya: can SE run a quick bench with our sample prompts? we can hand over a sanitized prompt set.
[00:05:33] Diego: absolutely. if you share the set and a short QPS profile we can simulate and give latency/cost estimates.
[00:05:41] Jules: would benching on hosted expose sample data? we prefer sanitized.
[00:05:45] Diego: use sanitized prompts or mocked PII and we'll run against a small private test account.
[00:05:52] Maya: next step we'll send the security pack and the bench template, and diego will run the bench once you share samples.
[00:05:59] Priya: sounds good. timeline—if we do hosted quicklaunch first, and it's promising, what's the path to move to dedicated?
[00:06:08] Maya: common path: start with hosted and quickstart credits -> validate product fit -> move to dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit) for predictable latency/cost -> optionally migrate to private/VPC for compliance. migration tools exist in console and we provide runbooks.
[00:06:24] Owen: is there any vendor lock if we move to dedicated? like, are model variants bound to your runtime?
[00:06:30] Diego: we support standard model formats, and you can pin versions. the runtime optimizes kernels but you can export model artifacts if needed, though operationally migration requires planning.
[00:06:43] Priya: what's the billing cadence for hosted? monthly?
[00:06:47] Maya: monthly billing with a usage invoice; for dedicated it's a committed monthly fee plus overage policies if you burst.
[00:06:56] Jules: do you provide audit logs for all API activity? retention configurable?
[00:07:00] Diego: yes, audit logs available; retention is configurable as an add-on for hosted, default is 30 days, enterprise plans can extend. Private you control retention.
[00:07:12] Owen: any gotchas around cold starts? we care about tail latency.
[00:07:16] Diego: cold starts can impact models with large KV caches; we mitigate with warming policies and reserve slots in dedicated pools. also continuous batching helps smooth tails.
[00:07:29] Priya: okay, let's talk practical TTFT—time to first token—what should our on-call engineer expect?
[00:07:35] Maya: with guided quickstart, examples, and the credit, many teams get to first token in under 2 hours. if you need a working assistant demo we can have you from zero to a basic end-to-end demo in a day including a simple web UI.
[00:07:50] Priya: good. we'll try to have an engineer redeem credits today.
[00:07:55] Owen: security asks—do you support IP whitelisting for API keys?
[00:07:59] Diego: yes IP allow lists, SSO, RBAC, and granular token scopes.
[00:08:06] Jules: what about data residency—we have EMEA customers and need EU data at rest.
[00:08:11] Maya: hosted can pin region to EU; we have EU regions and can arrange data residency for logs and storage.
[00:08:20] Priya: are there sample customer references for fintech? we want someone similar.
[00:08:24] Maya: i can share case study links; note some are NDAs so we'll provide public references plus a channel intro if you want.
[00:08:34] Owen: ok, on the cost model—can you share a sample cost calc for 30 rps and 200k tokens/day?
[00:08:40] Maya: yes, we'll send a simple calc in the pricing sheet.
[00:08:47] Priya: just to surface any blockers—our procurement requires SOC2 and an IP addendum. procurement timeline typically 3-6 weeks.
[00:08:56] Maya: understood. we'll include procurement-ready docs in the pack.
[00:09:02] Diego: one more technical note: if you want to test quantized model variants to reduce cost we can recommend profiles based on your prompt length distribution.
[00:09:12] Priya: that could be interesting—token length distribution is mostly short, 20-80 tokens.
[00:09:18] Diego: good candidate for 4-bit quantization variants — we'll note that for the bench.
[00:09:25] Maya: ok closing thoughts—any blockers to executing the quickstart this week?
[00:09:30] Priya: none, we'll try to redeem credits today and share sample prompts by tomorrow.
[00:09:35] Owen: i'll coordinate infra stuff and share IP/region constraints.
[00:09:40] Jules: i'll surface the exact compliance checklist items needed.
[00:09:44] Maya: great; we'll follow up with the pack and proposed times for the benchmark run. thanks all.
[00:09:51] Priya: thanks, talk soon.
[00:09:53] Maya: bye everyone.
---
